question: A man sells a bicycle for ₹990 at a loss of 10%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the bicycle to earn a profit of 24%?
solution:
Given:

Selling Price of an article = Rs. 990

Loss % = 10%

Formula used:

S.P = C.P (100 - Loss)/100

S.P = C.P (100 + Profit)/100

Where,

C.P = Cost Price of an article

S.P = Selling Price of an article

Calculation:

S.P = C.P (100 - Loss)/100

⇒ 990 = C.P (100 - 10)/100

⇒ C.P = 990/0.90

⇒ C.P = 1,100

Now to earn a profit of 24% the S.P:

S.P = 1100 (100 + 24)/100

⇒ S.P = 11 × 124

⇒ S.P = 1364

∴ The selling price of an article will be Rs. 1,364

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Using the fraction method,

10% = 1/10, 24% = 6/25

S.P = 990 × (10/9) × (31/25)

S.P = 1364
